claims.title: What does a deformation at the generic point of the special fibre remember?
claims.hypotheses: A smooth scheme over a discrete valuation ring and a local test ring centred at a generic point of the special fibre are given. The base maximal ideal maps to zero.
claims.statement: The map from the local test scheme factors through the residue field of that generic point. Two such factorizations can have different infinitesimal parts.

claims.title: Why is the geometric generic point ordinary at the chosen place?
claims.hypotheses: The canonical unitary moduli scheme has algebra degree one, admissible level and coefficient place. The refined torsion alternative, coefficient calculations, deformation realization and crystalline comparisons apply.
claims.statement: At any geometric generic point of a special component the distinguished torsion has Q^(n−1) geometric points.

claims.title: Which torsion points can be followed through reduction?
claims.hypotheses: The unitary datum has algebra degree one, the test valuation ring has algebraically closed fraction field with q nonzero, and the distinguished torsion is finite flat.
claims.statement: There are Q^n integral torsion sections. Restriction identifies them with the generic torsion and every special torsion point lifts.

claims.title: Why do points with the same reduction differ by exactly one line?
claims.hypotheses: The special point is ordinary, the torsion and isogeny comparisons apply, and the test valuation ring has algebraically closed fraction field.
claims.statement: Reduction has a one-dimensional kernel C independent of the Hecke index. Integral sections of the type-j correspondence correspond to j-dimensional subspaces of the common torsion space.

claims.title: Why do two lifts that avoid the ordinary line give the same reduced quotient?
claims.hypotheses: Two Hecke subspaces miss C and have the same image in the quotient by C. The marked polarized isogenies satisfy the distinguished-kernel and adjoint comparisons.
claims.statement: Their underlying reduced moduli targets agree, and every geometric source point has the same image over that target.

claims.title: Why does a lift containing the line produce a Frobenius twist?
claims.hypotheses: Two subspaces with the same quotient image differ in dimension by one and only the larger contains C. The one-dimensional local algebra and relative Frobenius comparisons hold.
claims.statement: The larger quotient has the same moduli target and point images as the smaller quotient followed by relative Frobenius, after the indicated target identification.

claims.title: How can residue points on the marked fibre power be compared?
claims.hypotheses: The marked correspondence has its Cartesian source and respects the level sections, and the universal family on the marked base is the pullback of the underlying one.
claims.statement: The same or twisted target equalities hold on the whole marked fibre power by testing all level sections and the individual fibre coordinates.

claims.title: Which residue target does the subspace count use?
claims.hypotheses: A valuation-ring test is centred at the generic point of the uniformizer divisor and the section comparison and marked quotient identities apply.
claims.statement: One value A(U) is defined independently of the complementary lift. Each section gives A(U) or its residue twist. The even and odd multisets therefore agree at each target.
